items.title: Insurers Are Undermining the No Surprises Act and Then Claiming the IDR Process Is Broken, New Analysis Sent to Congress Explains | Newswise - Newswise
items.reason: This item directly addresses alleged insurer practices undermining the No Surprises Act and discusses problems with the IDR process, which are core components of No Surprises Act implementation and enforcement.
items.summary: A new analysis sent to Congress alleges that insurers are systematically undermining the No Surprises Act's balance-billing protections while simultaneously claiming the Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process is broken—essentially creating the problems they blame on the system itself. The analysis appears to document specific insurer practices that circumvent the law's protections, then use disputes over the IDR process to avoid accountability. This development is significant for revenue-cycle teams because it reveals potential enforcement gaps in the IDR mechanism and identifies strategic insurer behaviors that may affect payment outcomes and balance-billing case resolutions. Congressional awareness of these allegations could prompt regulatory action or legislative clarification regarding IDR procedures and insurer compliance obligations.
